answer.summary: No peer-reviewed primary-source evidence was retrieved to support claims about tokenized agent memory retention under intermittent input streams with known perturbations and bounded token budgets.
answer.content: No verifiable peer-reviewed studies or primary-source datasets were found that provide time-series metrics on output token coherence, decay rates, or state drift in tokenized agents under intermittent, perturbed input streams with bounded token budgets. The investigation confirms the absence of direct, empirical data matching the required criteria for comparative analysis with continuous static baselines. All claims about memory superiority remain ungrounded without such time-series, controlled-input evidence. A search was conducted but no sources met the specified criteria; no source IDs were retrieved to validate or support the research premise. This absence does not imply the phenomenon is unmeasurable, only that no such data is currently available in the accessible literature. The research question cannot be answered with current evidence, and further investigation must be grounded in direct, empirical findings before comparative analysis can proceed.
answer.nextTask: Identify and retrieve a peer-reviewed study with explicit time-series metrics on tokenized agent memory retention under intermittent input streams and known perturbations, including per-interval coherence scores and state drift indicators under bounded token budget
answer.lesson: All claims about agent memory performance must be anchored in direct, verifiable time-series data from peer-reviewed studies with explicit decay and coherence metrics under controlled input conditions before comparative analysis can proceed; absence of such data invalidates the research premise and requires revision of scope
